reason: Passes the feasibility/schedule check. (1) It is a lab-only rule. tools/trainlab.py already replays dc0.15/0.20/0.30/0.35 on CPU from the presafe graph using recorded DeepCenter scores (l.512-520). For each stem and arm it stores new_forks/gone_forks against control, keyed by parent id, plus official TP/FP fork labels from score_divisions (l.429-463, 525-538), all written to results.json (l.777). The marginal set, evaluable = (new or gone) ∩ (TP ∪ FP), and the Wilson 80% bounds are a ~50-line post-hoc CPU function. It needs no kernel change, no GPU and no rerun of exp60, and can sit in a separate script so trainlab.py and its 69 tests stay untouched. (2) Runtime is 0: K3b only changes DEEPCENTER_SAFE_DIV_THRESHOLD over scores that are already computed, so it adds nothing against the ~4 h headroom. Off equals x138 byte for byte (t = 0.25, no build if t* = 0.25), and dummy gate 5 (node set == K3) stays. (3) The LB path fits: S5 is 26 Sep 11:00-14:00 UTC, so the score arrives around 18:00-22:00 UTC 26 Sep, before the R8 cutoff at 27 Sep 12:00. The likely result is that fewer than 6 evaluable marginal forks turn up in 6bba CONFIRMATION (20 clips, 45 GT divisions, ~3.3% evaluable). K3b then is not built, which frees S5 and ~0.7 GPU-h of dummy time. (4) The binding risk is timing, not code. CONTEXT.md l.1824 says exp60 shard A was pushed at 17:15 UTC (done ~19:15) and shard B after FF, with the T9 audit moved to TONIGHT. The rule is therefore only pre-registered if its text is committed before anyone runs `trainlab.py score` on shard outputs. If that is missed, D3 becomes a post-hoc gate change and must be dropped. (5) The idea's premise is partly wrong. The coded gate already has a precision clause, new_fork_precision_ge_0.35 (l.649), but it divides by ALL new forks, non-evaluable ones included. That makes it close to unpassable when lowering t and VACUOUS when raising t (new_forks is empty, so the check sees None and passes). D3 fixes the raise direction. But since D3 'replaces' the gate and drops conf >= +0.002 and the plateau check, it could be LOOSER than the coded gate in the add direction, so it should be ANDed with the existing checks, not substituted for them.
fix: Before `trainlab.py score` is run on any exp60 shard output (so by ~19:15 UTC 25 Sep), commit the exact rule text to CONTEXT.md with a timestamp. The rule: direction picked by the sign of the pooled 6bba SELECTION delta. On 6bba CONFIRMATION, evaluable marginal forks = (new_forks or gone_forks) ∩ (tp_forks ∪ fp_forks) of the arm/control. Require n_eval >= 6 plus a Wilson 80% (z = 1.2816) LB > 0.265 when adding or UB < 0.167 when removing, together with 44b6 delta >= -0.0005, |adj_edge delta| <= 0.0005, nodes unchanged, and dc_miss == 0 on 6bba (or say that the marginal set is partial). AND this with the existing checks (conf >= +0.002, plateau, fork change <= +50%) rather than replacing them. Implement it afterwards as a separate read-only script over results.json (e.g. tools/dc_marginal.py plus one unit test on a synthetic results.json), leaving trainlab.py and its gates unchanged. Keep K3b's LB acceptance under R4.
realistic_gain: Implementation 0.5-1 h of CPU, 0 GPU, 0 hidden-run time. Expected LB value is mostly avoided loss, about +0.0002 to +0.0005 in expectation (it blocks a 1-event false pass worth -0.001 to -0.002 public). The more concrete gain is scheduling: most likely (>~70%) the gate says no, K3b is dropped early, and S5 plus ~0.7 GPU-h of dummy time are freed for K3/K4 on 26 Sep. If it passes (~0.10-0.15), the center is about +0.001 public, and it is still only accepted by R4.
